relations.myth: The Goddess slays the shape-changing buffalo asura
relations.note: She pins him underfoot, spears him, and beheads his emerging form.

relations.myth: Battle after Mahiṣa's conquest of heaven
relations.note: He battles the Goddess in buffalo, lion, human, and elephant forms.

relations.myth: Indigenous king defeated through a woman's deception
relations.note: Modern counter-narratives say invaders sent Durgā to deceive the indigenous ruler.
relations.source: Modern Bahujan oral and activist accounts

relations.myth: Woman sent to seduce the indigenous king
relations.note: Some modern counter-narratives say Durgā seduced him because men could not defeat him.
relations.source: Modern Bahujan oral and activist accounts

relations.myth: Century-long war against Indra's gods
relations.note: Mahiṣa defeats Indra's divine forces after a war lasting one hundred years.

relations.myth: Usurpation of Indra's office
relations.note: After defeating the gods, Mahiṣa assumes Indra's kingship and authority.

relations.myth: Appropriation of the gods' offices
relations.note: Mahiṣa appropriates Sūrya's solar authority after conquering heaven.

relations.myth: Appropriation of the gods' offices
relations.note: Mahiṣa appropriates Agni's divine authority after conquering heaven.

relations.myth: Agni's boon leads to Mahiṣa's birth
relations.note: Agni grants Rambha the powerful son whose buffalo parentage produces Mahiṣa.

relations.myth: Appropriation of the gods' offices
relations.note: Mahiṣa appropriates Vāyu's authority after conquering heaven.

relations.myth: Appropriation of the gods' offices
relations.note: Mahiṣa appropriates Candra's lunar authority after conquering heaven.

relations.myth: Appropriation of the gods' offices
relations.note: Mahiṣa appropriates Yama's authority over death after conquering heaven.

relations.myth: Appropriation of the gods' offices
relations.note: Mahiṣa appropriates Varuṇa's authority after conquering heaven.

relations.myth: Creation of the Goddess from divine radiance
relations.note: Brahmā's radiance helps form the Goddess raised against Mahiṣa.

relations.myth: Boon protecting Mahiṣa from male killers
relations.note: Brahmā grants protection against males, leaving a woman able to kill him.

relations.myth: Creation of the Goddess from divine radiance
relations.note: Viṣṇu's anger at Mahiṣa emits radiance and he arms the Goddess.

relations.myth: Creation of the Goddess from divine radiance
relations.note: Śiva's anger at Mahiṣa emits radiance and he gives the Goddess a trident.

relations.myth: Mahiṣa as Śiva's devotee
relations.note: South Indian variants portray Mahiṣa as Śiva's devotee, complicating his killing.

relations.myth: Gods equip the Goddess for war
relations.note: Himavat gives the Goddess her lion and jewels for the war against Mahiṣa.

relations.myth: Gods equip the Goddess for war
relations.note: Kubera supplies the drinking vessel used by Mahiṣa's divine opponent.

relations.myth: Gods equip the Goddess for war
relations.note: Śeṣa gives Mahiṣa's divine opponent a jeweled serpent necklace.
Mahiṣa is born as Rambha's shape-changing buffalo son.

relations.myth: Birth following the buffalo-mother's self-immolation
relations.note: Mahiṣa emerges through Rambha's union and the buffalo-mother's funeral-pyre death.
Karambha is Rambha's brother and thus Mahiṣa's paternal uncle.

relations.myth: Kātyāyanī battles the buffalo asura
relations.note: The goddess associated with Kātyāyana's hermitage fights Mahiṣa.

relations.myth: Kātyāyanī slays Mahiṣa
relations.note: The Kātyāyanī manifestation kills Mahiṣa in this Purāṇic version.

relations.myth: Mahiṣa approaches the ascetic goddess
relations.note: Mahiṣa desires or approaches Pārvatī, provoking her manifested warrior form.

relations.myth: Warrior manifestation destroys Mahiṣa
relations.note: Pārvatī destroys him through her manifested warrior form.

relations.myth: Skanda kills a possibly identical Mahiṣa
relations.note: Some traditions attribute the killing to Skanda, though the demon's identity is disputed.

relations.myth: Nandā kills Mahiṣa in the Vindhyas
relations.note: Regional Purāṇic versions assign Mahiṣa's death to Nandā.
Some conflicting medieval genealogies describe Raktabīja as Mahiṣa's close associate.
Later Ayyappa traditions identify the buffalo-demoness Mahīṣī as Mahiṣāsura's sister.

relations.myth: Recurrent buffalo conflict in another cosmic cycle
relations.note: Ugracaṇḍā kills a form of Mahiṣa in one recurring cosmic cycle.

relations.myth: Recurrent buffalo conflict in another cosmic cycle
relations.note: Bhadrakālī kills a form of Mahiṣa in one recurring cosmic cycle.
